Sears had Amazon's playbook. A century early.
A watch seller becomes a mail-order empire.
By 1894 the catalog sold sewing machines and baby carriages.
Insurance and credit too: Allstate and Discover.
It built the world's tallest building.
Then it stopped mailing the catalog.
Sears didn't lack the idea. It already had it.
Protect the customer habit, not the format.
